meaning: cepedianus: for Comte de La Cépède (1756–1825), French naturalist
description: A stout silver-grey to brown shark with a broad, blunt head, small eyes and seven pairs of gill slits, where most sharks have five. Small black spots, and some white ones, are scattered over the back and flanks, and a single dorsal fin sits far back above a long tail. It hunts in bays and over shallow shelves, taking other sharks, rays, bony fishes and seals, and sometimes hunts in groups.
depth: Surface to about 570 m, mostly shallower than 136 m
eats: Other sharks, rays, bony fishes, seals and dolphins, and carrion
